title: Quantitative ML Research, Market Regime Discovery, Visual DAG Compiler & 1:1 Replay Platform
whyParagraphs: Algorithmic trading research usually breaks in four predictable ways: standard cross-validation leaks overlapping future price windows into training sets; strategy logic written in Python notebooks diverges from TypeScript execution code; gradient-boosted trees overfit noisy features without calibrated linear benchmarks; and static thresholds collapse when market regimes shift.
Trade Bot was built as a strict, leakage-proof research and replay platform where ML models, unsupervised regime mining, visual graph compilation, and execution parity share deterministic contracts.
scopeDisclaimer: Scope Notice: All public architecture and evaluation diagrams document ML validation methodology, data engineering, and deterministic execution parity only. No proprietary strategy parameters or financial return claims are presented.

subsystems.title: Columnar & Relational Lakehouse with Lineage Pinning
subsystems.summary: Enforces strict Binance USD-M Futures venue isolation and SHA-256 dataset digests across Parquet, DuckDB, PostgreSQL, and Redis.
bullets: Market data ingests strictly from Binance USD-M Futures APIs and Vision archives into SHA-256 pinned Parquet corpora, failing closed on mixed-venue or unverified datasets.

Analytical workloads query multi-gigabyte archives via DuckDB 1.5.5, PyArrow 16.1, Pandas, and NumPy, while discovery_dataset_rows, trade lifecycle snapshots, and optimizer queues persist in PostgreSQL, SQLite (better-sqlite3), and Redis (ioredis).

subsystems.title: Oracle Supervised ML & Purged Walk-Forward Validation
subsystems.summary: Benchmarks depth-constrained LightGBM challengers against Scikit-Learn linear baselines under episode-grouped embargo folds.
bullets: Inside the Oracle pipeline, LightGBM 4.6 (LGBMClassifier and LGBMRegressor) challengers benchmark directly against Scikit-Learn 1.9 baselines (SimpleImputer -> StandardScaler -> LogisticRegression) and historical priors.

Expanding temporal quantile splits enforce outcomeAvailableAt < fold_start with a PURGE_4H_MS embargo buffer and episode grouping (symbol|episodeId). A programmatic assertion aborts any run if set(train.group) & set(test.group) is non-empty, evaluating models on out-of-sample ROC-AUC, Log-Loss calibration, and net-of-fee/slippage/funding replay.

subsystems.title: Wave Y Unsupervised Market Regime Discovery
subsystems.summary: Discovers density-based market regimes via UMAP + HDBSCAN on 30+ point-in-time features with ablation and OOS portability checks.
bullets: Wave Y scales 30+ point-in-time microstructural and cross-asset features (trend persistence, structural churn, taker buy/sell imbalance, volatility compression, BTC/ETH leadership, and sector relative strength) strictly on in-sample cutoffs.

Features project through UMAP into HDBSCAN 0.8.33 density clusters with explicit noise separation, followed by feature ablation (hl02), radius sensitivity sweeps (hl01), counterfactual attribution, and out-of-sample portability validation.

subsystems.title: Visual DAG Strategy Compiler & 1:1 Replay Parity
subsystems.summary: Compiles React Flow strategy graphs through AJV schemas into a single TypeScript kernel shared across Backtest, Replay, Paper, and Live.
bullets: A visual node-graph editor built with React 18, @xyflow/react (React Flow v12), Dagre, Zustand, and TradingView Lightweight Charts compiles strategy graphs through AJV JSON Schema validation and updateBlockLogicManifest.ts checks into deterministic runtime ASTs.

Backtesting, historical replay harnesses (proc204 and proc206), paper simulation, and live runtime (Express 5, WebSockets ws, CCXT) execute the exact same decision kernel, with mode differences confined strictly to clock and broker adapters.
